title: God Is the Judge
superscription: For the choirmaster: To the tune of "Do Not Destroy." A Psalm of Asaph. A song.

verses.text: We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near. The people declare Your wondrous works.
"When I choose a time, I will judge fairly.
When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars. Selah
I say to the proud, 'Do not boast,' and to the wicked, 'Do not lift up your horn.
Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak with an outstretched neck.'"
For exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert,
but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another.
For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours from His cup, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs.
But I will proclaim Him forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
"All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted."

context.author: Asaph, one of David’s chief musicians; his family led Temple singing for centuries (Ezra 2:41). Book Three (Psalms 73-89) opens with eleven psalms of Asaph (73-83), several of which mourn the fall of Jerusalem or of the northern kingdom, so many were written or adapted by later members of his guild.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, in times of national crisis
context.setting: “We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near” (v.1). Then God speaks: “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly. When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars” (vv.2-3). He warns the proud, “Do not lift up your horn” (vv.4-5). “For exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert, but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another” (vv.6-7). “A cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine… all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs” (v.8). The singer will praise the God of Jacob, and God ends: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted” (v.10).
context.custom: A horn, like a wild ox’s, stood for strength and pride; to lift it was to boast. The earth was pictured as resting on pillars (1 Samuel 2:8). The cup of wrath was mixed wine that made the drinker stagger, a picture of judgment (Jeremiah 25:15).
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 76 celebrates God who broke the weapons of war at Salem.
context.timelineBible: Hannah sang, “He humbles and He exalts” (1 Samuel 2:7). Mary sang, “He has brought down rulers from their thrones, but has exalted the humble” (Luke 1:52). In Gethsemane Jesus prayed, “Let this cup pass from Me” (Matthew 26:39), the cup of judgment He drank for others.

translation.meaning: Cup; one’s lot, often of judgment.

Let this cup pass from Me.

The cup of the wine of wrath.
You who drank the cup of His fury.

overview.summary: God declares that He will judge at His appointed time; exaltation comes from Him alone, the proud will drink His cup of wrath, and the righteous will be lifted up.
overview.settingLine: The earth shaking on its pillars.

archaeology.t: Horns on altar corners stood for power and refuge.
Painted Iron Age cups and kraters for mixing wine.

overview.discussion: “Exaltation comes neither from east nor west… but it is God who judges” (vv.6-7). Where am I looking for promotion or recognition?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Asaph
